problem.title: Roots of x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0
problem.statement: Find the roots of the equation x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0.
hints: Which two numbers multiply to 6 and add to -5?
Both numbers are negative because the product is positive and the sum is negative.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: A quadratic with a = 1; we need its two roots.

steps.label: Find
steps.content: Values of x that satisfy the equation

steps.label: Concept
steps.content: Factorisation by splitting the middle term

steps.label: Method
steps.content: Find p, q with p x q = a x c = 6 and p + q = -5

commonMistakes.description: Read the constant term as the root.

coach.hint: Look for two numbers whose product is 6 and whose sum is -5. Start by listing factor pairs of 6.
coach.concept: This is a quadratic in standard form with a = 1. The concept is factorisation by splitting the middle term: rewrite -5x as two terms so you can group.
coach.guide: Plan: 1) list factor pairs of 6, 2) pick the pair adding to -5, 3) rewrite the middle term, 4) group and factor, 5) set each bracket to zero.
coach.checkApproach: If you found the pair -2 and -3 you are on the right track. Check that you set each factor equal to zero rather than the whole expression.
coach.findMistake: The usual slip is the sign: the product is +6 so both numbers share a sign, and the sum -5 forces both negative. Roots are then +2 and +3, not -2 and -3.
coach.fullExplanation: x^2 - 5x + 6 = x^2 - 2x - 3x + 6 = x(x - 2) - 3(x - 2) = (x - 2)(x - 3). Setting each factor to zero gives x = 2 or x = 3. Substituting back confirms both.

problem.title: Roots of x^2 + 7x + 10 = 0
problem.statement: Solve x^2 + 7x + 10 = 0 by factorisation.

steps.label: Method
steps.content: Numbers with product 10 and sum 7: 2 and 5

coach.hint: Find two numbers with product 10 and sum 7.
coach.concept: Factorisation of a monic quadratic: split 7x using two numbers that multiply to 10.
coach.guide: List factor pairs of 10 (1,10), (2,5). Which pair sums to 7? Then write the brackets and solve.
coach.checkApproach: Good if you reached (x + 2)(x + 5). Each bracket equal to zero gives a negative root.
coach.findMistake: When the bracket is (x + 2), the root is x = -2, not +2. Flip the sign when reading roots off brackets.

problem.title: Roots of x^2 - 9 = 0
problem.statement: Find the roots of x^2 - 9 = 0.
hints: x^2 - 9 is a difference of two squares.
Two roots, one positive and one negative.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: There is no x term, so b = 0.

coach.hint: Can you write 9 as a square? Then use a^2 - b^2.
coach.concept: The concept is the difference of squares identity a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b).
coach.guide: Write x^2 - 3^2, apply the identity, then set each bracket to zero.
coach.checkApproach: If you took the square root of both sides, remember a square root equation has two answers.
coach.findMistake: Taking sqrt 9 = 3 alone misses the negative root. Both 3 and -3 square to 9.

problem.title: Roots of 2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0
problem.statement: Solve 2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0.
problem.concept: Splitting the middle term when a is not 1
hints: The product to use is a x c = 6, not 3.
Which two numbers multiply to 6 and add to -7?

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: a = 2, so the product for splitting is a x c.

steps.label: Method
steps.content: Numbers with product 6 and sum -7: -6 and -1

commonMistakes.description: Used product c = 3 instead of a x c = 6.

coach.hint: Since a = 2, multiply a and c first: 2 x 3 = 6. Now find two numbers with product 6 and sum -7.
coach.concept: Splitting the middle term still works when a is not 1, but the product you need is a x c.
coach.guide: 1) Compute a x c = 6. 2) Find the pair with sum -7. 3) Rewrite -7x. 4) Factor by grouping. 5) Solve each bracket, remembering 2x - 1 = 0 gives x = 1/2.
coach.checkApproach: If you used -6 and -1 and grouped to get (2x - 1)(x - 3), you are correct. Double-check the root from 2x - 1 = 0.
coach.findMistake: Most errors here come from using product 3 instead of 6, or from solving 2x - 1 = 0 as x = 2 instead of x = 1/2.

problem.title: Roots of 3x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0
problem.statement: Find the roots of 3x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0.
problem.concept: Splitting the middle term when a is not 1

coach.hint: Multiply a and c: 3 x (-1) = -3. Find numbers with product -3 and sum -2.
coach.concept: Factorisation with a = 3: the split uses a x c.
coach.guide: Compute a x c, choose the pair (-3, 1), rewrite the middle term, group, then solve 3x + 1 = 0 and x - 1 = 0.
coach.checkApproach: If you have (3x + 1)(x - 1), just read the roots carefully: 3x + 1 = 0 gives x = -1/3.
coach.findMistake: Check the sign of the fractional root: 3x + 1 = 0 means 3x = -1, so x = -1/3, not +1/3.

problem.title: Consecutive integers with product 306
problem.statement: Find two consecutive positive integers whose product is 306.
hints: Let the smaller integer be x. The next one is x + 1.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Two unknowns that differ by 1; one variable suffices.

steps.label: Given
steps.content: Product of x and x + 1 is 306

commonMistakes.description: Answered only the equation's root 17 without the second integer.

coach.hint: Call the smaller number x. What is the next integer, and what is their product?
coach.concept: This is a word problem that forms a quadratic: x(x + 1) = 306.
coach.guide: 1) Set x(x + 1) = 306. 2) Rearrange to x^2 + x - 306 = 0. 3) Split using 18 and -17. 4) Solve. 5) Reject the negative root since the integers are positive.
coach.checkApproach: If your equation is x^2 + x - 306 = 0 you are right. Make sure you answered with both integers.
coach.findMistake: The question asks for two integers, and the negative root must be rejected. The answer is 17 and 18.
coach.fullExplanation: x(x + 1) = 306 gives x^2 + x - 306 = 0 = (x + 18)(x - 17). x = 17 since it must be positive, so the integers are 17 and 18.

problem.title: Roots of x^2 + 2x - 1 = 0
problem.statement: Solve x^2 + 2x - 1 = 0. Give exact roots.
hints: No integer pair has product -1 and sum 2, so use the formula.
sqrt 8 = 2 sqrt 2, then divide the whole numerator by 2.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Middle term will not split over integers.

commonMistakes.description: Forgot to divide the sqrt term by 2.

coach.hint: Try to split 2x with product -1: it does not work, so reach for the formula.
coach.concept: When factorisation fails, the quadratic formula always applies. Compute the discriminant first.
coach.guide: 1) Identify a, b, c. 2) D = 4 + 4 = 8. 3) Substitute into the formula. 4) Simplify sqrt 8. 5) Divide every term of the numerator by 2.
coach.checkApproach: If you got (-2 +/- sqrt 8)/2 you are almost there: simplify sqrt 8 = 2 sqrt 2 and divide both terms.
coach.findMistake: Common errors: writing +2 instead of -2 for -b, or dividing only the first term of the numerator by 2.

problem.title: Value of k from a known root
problem.statement: If x = 2 is a root of x^2 + kx - 10 = 0, find k and the other root.
hints: A root satisfies the equation: substitute x = 2.
Then the product of roots is -10.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: A root makes the equation true.

steps.label: Method
steps.content: Substitute x = 2 to get k; product of roots = c/a = -10

coach.hint: What does it mean for x = 2 to be a root? Put 2 in place of x.
coach.concept: Two concepts: a root satisfies the equation, and the product of roots equals c/a.
coach.guide: 1) Substitute x = 2 and solve for k. 2) Use product of roots = -10 to get the other root. 3) Answer both parts.
coach.checkApproach: If you found k = 3, now find the second root: 2 x (other) = -10.
coach.findMistake: Watch signs when substituting: 2^2 + k(2) - 10 = 0 gives 2k = 6. And remember the question asks for the other root too.
coach.fullExplanation: Substitute x = 2: 4 + 2k - 10 = 0, k = 3. Then x^2 + 3x - 10 = (x + 5)(x - 2), so the other root is -5.

problem.title: Rectangle from area and difference
problem.statement: A rectangular field has area 60 m^2 and its length is 7 m more than its breadth. Find the breadth.
hints: Let breadth be b, then length is b + 7.
One root is negative and must be rejected.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Two dimensions linked by a difference; area gives the equation.

commonMistakes.description: Reported the length 12 instead of the breadth.

coach.hint: Choose the breadth as your unknown and write the length in terms of it.
coach.concept: Area of a rectangle equals length x breadth; that gives the quadratic.
coach.guide: 1) b(b + 7) = 60. 2) b^2 + 7b - 60 = 0. 3) Factor. 4) Reject the negative root. 5) Report the breadth in metres.
coach.checkApproach: If you reached (b + 12)(b - 5), pick the root that makes sense for a length.
coach.findMistake: A length cannot be negative, so -12 is rejected. Also check the question asks for the breadth, not the length.
coach.fullExplanation: b(b + 7) = 60 gives b^2 + 7b - 60 = 0 = (b + 12)(b - 5). b = 5, so breadth is 5 m (length 12 m).

problem.title: Train speed from a time difference
problem.statement: A train covers 480 km at a uniform speed. If the speed were 8 km/h less, it would take 3 hours more. Find the original speed.
problem.concept: Time = distance / speed, forming a quadratic
hints: Let the speed be x km/h. Time = 480/x.
Slower time minus faster time equals 3: 480/(x - 8) - 480/x = 3.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Speed change produces a time change; use time = distance / speed.

steps.label: Given
steps.content: Distance 480 km; speed reduced by 8 km/h adds 3 h

steps.label: Concept
steps.content: Rational equation leading to a quadratic

commonMistakes.description: Set 480/x - 480/(x - 8) = 3 and got a negative speed.

coach.hint: Write the time for each speed as distance over speed. Which time is longer?
coach.concept: Time = distance / speed. The slower journey takes 3 h longer, so subtract the two times.
coach.guide: 1) Times 480/x and 480/(x - 8). 2) Slower minus faster = 3. 3) Multiply out to get a quadratic. 4) Factor. 5) Reject the negative root.
coach.checkApproach: If your equation is 480/(x - 8) - 480/x = 3, multiply through by x(x - 8) and simplify to x^2 - 8x - 1280 = 0.
coach.findMistake: Typical slips: subtracting in the wrong order (sign error), or answering the slower speed 32 instead of the original 40.

problem.title: Sum of reciprocals
problem.statement: Find the roots of the equation 1/(x - 1) + 1/(x + 1) = 3/4.
hints: Combine the fractions on the left: (x + 1 + x - 1)/(x^2 - 1).

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Two fractions with x in the denominator.

coach.hint: Add the two fractions using the common denominator (x - 1)(x + 1).
coach.concept: Combine fractions, then cross-multiply to reach a quadratic.
coach.guide: 1) Common denominator x^2 - 1. 2) Numerator 2x. 3) Cross-multiply. 4) Rearrange to 3x^2 - 8x - 3 = 0. 5) Split with -9 and 1.
coach.checkApproach: If you have 8x = 3(x^2 - 1) you are on track. Rearrange carefully.
coach.findMistake: Check the numerator: (x + 1) + (x - 1) = 2x, not 2. And keep the sign of -8x when rearranging.
coach.fullExplanation: 2x/(x^2 - 1) = 3/4, so 8x = 3x^2 - 3, 3x^2 - 8x - 3 = 0 = (3x + 1)(x - 3). Roots 3 and -1/3, neither makes a denominator zero.

problem.title: Two pipes filling a tank
problem.statement: Two pipes together fill a tank in 6 hours. The larger pipe alone takes 5 hours less than the smaller one. How long does the smaller pipe take alone?
hints: Let the smaller pipe take x hours; the larger takes x - 5.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Rates of work add when pipes work together.

steps.label: Given
steps.content: Together 6 h; larger is 5 h faster

steps.label: Find
steps.content: Time for the smaller pipe alone

steps.label: Solve
steps.content: (x - 15)(x - 2) = 0; x = 2 is rejected since x - 5 would be negative

coach.hint: Think in rates: a pipe that fills in x hours fills 1/x of the tank per hour.
coach.concept: Combined rate equals the sum of individual rates.
coach.guide: 1) Rates 1/x and 1/(x - 5). 2) Sum equals 1/6. 3) Multiply through. 4) Solve the quadratic. 5) Reject the root that makes x - 5 negative.
coach.checkApproach: If you reached x^2 - 17x + 30 = 0, both roots are positive, so use the extra condition x > 5.
coach.findMistake: x = 2 gives the larger pipe -3 hours, impossible. And the question asks for the smaller pipe (15 h), not the larger (10 h).
coach.fullExplanation: 1/x + 1/(x - 5) = 1/6 leads to x^2 - 17x + 30 = 0 = (x - 15)(x - 2). x = 15 hours for the smaller pipe, 10 hours for the larger.

problem.title: Roots that are reciprocals
problem.statement: For what value of k are the roots of (k + 1)x^2 - 6x + 3k = 0 reciprocals of each other?

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: A condition on the roots translates to a condition on coefficients.

commonMistakes.description: Used sum of roots = 1 instead of product.

coach.hint: If the roots are alpha and 1/alpha, what is their product?
coach.concept: Reciprocal roots means product of roots = 1, and product = c/a.
coach.guide: 1) Write product = 3k/(k + 1). 2) Set equal to 1. 3) Solve the linear equation. 4) Confirm a = k + 1 is non-zero and D >= 0.
coach.checkApproach: If you set 3k/(k + 1) = 1 you are correct; solve carefully.
coach.findMistake: The trap is using the sum of roots. Reciprocals do not have a fixed sum; they have product 1.
coach.fullExplanation: Product of roots = 3k/(k + 1) = 1 gives 3k = k + 1, k = 1/2. Check: D = 36 - 4(3/2)(3/2) = 27 > 0, so real roots exist.

problem.title: Sum of squares of roots
problem.statement: If alpha and beta are the roots of x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0, find alpha^2 + beta^2.
hints: You do not need the actual roots.

steps.label: Understand
steps.content: Ask for an expression in the roots, not the roots themselves.

steps.label: Concept
steps.content: Sum and product of roots with an identity

commonMistakes.description: Used (alpha + beta)^2 without subtracting 2 alpha beta.

coach.hint: Can you express alpha^2 + beta^2 using alpha + beta and alpha beta?
coach.concept: Symmetric expressions in roots can be built from sum and product without solving.
coach.guide: 1) Sum = -b/a = 5. 2) Product = c/a = 3. 3) Use the identity (alpha + beta)^2 - 2 alpha beta. 4) Compute.
coach.checkApproach: If you wrote 25 - 2 x 3 you are done: 19.
coach.findMistake: The most common error is forgetting the -2 alpha beta term, which gives 25.
coach.fullExplanation: alpha + beta = 5, alpha beta = 3. alpha^2 + beta^2 = 5^2 - 2 x 3 = 19.

problem.title: Common root of two quadratics
problem.statement: The equations x^2 + ax + 12 = 0 and x^2 + bx + 3 = 0 have a common root 3. Find a + b.

coach.hint: Substitute x = 3 into each equation separately.
coach.concept: A common root satisfies both equations, so substitution gives two simple linear equations.
coach.checkApproach: If you found a = -7 and b = -4, add them.
coach.findMistake: Sign care: 3a = -21 gives a = -7, not 7. Then a + b = -11.
coach.fullExplanation: From the first: 3a = -21, a = -7. From the second: 3b = -12, b = -4. a + b = -11.

problem.title: Final velocity after 5 seconds
problem.statement: A body travels with initial velocity 10 m/s and acceleration 2 m/s^2 for 5 seconds. Find its final velocity.
hints: Which equation connects u, a, t and v?
Multiply a by t first, then add u.

steps.label: Concept
steps.content: Equations of motion with uniform acceleration

steps.label: Diagram
steps.content: A straight line; body moving right, acceleration in the same direction

commonMistakes.description: Used s = ut + 1/2 at^2 and reported the displacement 75.
Added instead of multiplying a and t.

coach.hint: You know u, a and t and want v. Which equation has exactly those four letters?
coach.concept: This is uniform acceleration in a straight line, so the first equation of motion v = u + at applies.
coach.guide: 1) List u, a, t. 2) Pick v = u + at. 3) Substitute. 4) Multiply a x t first. 5) Add u. 6) Write the unit.
coach.checkApproach: If you wrote v = 10 + 2 x 5 you are correct. Compute and state the unit.
coach.findMistake: If you got 75, you used the displacement equation: that gives distance, not velocity. If you got 0 or -20 you flipped the sign of a, but the body is speeding up.
coach.fullExplanation: v = u + at = 10 + (2)(5) = 10 + 10 = 20 m/s. Units check: m/s.

problem.title: Convert 54 km/h to m/s
problem.statement: Express a speed of 54 km/h in m/s.

steps.label: Unit Check
steps.content: km/h x (1000 m / 3600 s) gives m/s

coach.hint: Replace km with 1000 m and h with 3600 s.
coach.concept: Converting units: km/h to m/s multiplies by 1000/3600 = 5/18.
coach.guide: 1) Write 54 km/h as 54 x 1000 m / 3600 s. 2) Simplify. 3) State m/s.
coach.checkApproach: If you multiplied by 5/18 you are right.
coach.findMistake: Multiplying by 18/5 goes the wrong way (m/s to km/h). 54 x 5/18 = 15.

problem.title: Distance during acceleration
problem.statement: A car moving at 20 m/s accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s^2 for 10 s. How far does it travel in this time?
hints: You have u, a, t and want s.

steps.label: Concept
steps.content: Uniform acceleration, displacement in time t

coach.hint: You want displacement from u, a, t. Which equation has s and t but not v?
coach.concept: The second equation of motion gives displacement under uniform acceleration.
coach.guide: 1) List u, a, t. 2) Use s = ut + (1/2)at^2. 3) Compute ut. 4) Compute (1/2)at^2 with t squared. 5) Add.
coach.checkApproach: If you have 200 + 100 you are right.
coach.findMistake: 400 means the half was dropped; 200 means the acceleration term was skipped.

problem.title: Stopping distance of a bike
problem.statement: A bike moving at 15 m/s applies brakes producing a retardation of 3 m/s^2. Find the distance covered before it stops.
problem.concept: Third equation of motion with negative acceleration
hints: Final velocity is 0 when it stops.
Time is not given, so use v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

steps.label: Diagram
steps.content: Bike moving right, acceleration pointing left

commonMistakes.description: Took a = +3 and got a negative distance.
Used s = ut + 1/2 at^2 with t = 5 assumed.

coach.hint: What is the final velocity of a bike that has stopped? And which equation avoids time?
coach.concept: When time is unknown, v^2 = u^2 + 2as connects the velocities to the distance. Brakes give negative a.
coach.guide: 1) v = 0, u = 15, a = -3. 2) Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as. 3) Substitute with the sign of a. 4) Solve for s. 5) Check the unit.
coach.checkApproach: If your line reads 0 = 225 - 6s you are correct.
coach.findMistake: A negative distance means the sign of a was wrong: retardation is negative when motion is positive. Also 2as means 2 x 3 = 6, not 3.

problem.title: Ball thrown upward
problem.statement: A ball is thrown vertically upward with speed 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, find the maximum height reached.
hints: At the top the velocity is zero.
Take upward as positive, so a = -10 m/s^2.

steps.label: Given
steps.content: u = 20 m/s, v = 0 at the top, a = -10 m/s^2

steps.label: Diagram
steps.content: Ball moving up, g pointing down

commonMistakes.description: Used a = +10 giving a negative height.
Used h = ut giving 40 with t = 2 s and no gravity term.

coach.hint: What is the velocity at the highest point?
coach.concept: Gravity is a uniform acceleration of 10 m/s^2 downward. Choose up as positive.
coach.guide: 1) v = 0 at the top. 2) a = -10. 3) v^2 = u^2 + 2as. 4) Solve for s.
coach.checkApproach: If you wrote 0 = 400 - 20h you are right.
coach.findMistake: A negative height signals a sign error in g. Height should come out positive with a = -10.

problem.title: Balance the iron and steam reaction
problem.statement: Balance the equation Fe + H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2 and give the coefficient of H2O.
hints: Balance Fe first: 3 Fe on the right.
Then O: 4 oxygens on the right.

steps.label: Property
steps.content: Atoms must balance on both sides

commonMistakes.description: Changed the subscript of water instead of the coefficient.
Balanced O but not H, giving 4H2 missing.

coach.hint: Start with the element that appears in only one compound on each side: iron.
coach.concept: Balancing means equal atoms of each element on both sides, adjusted only with coefficients.
coach.guide: 1) 3Fe for Fe3O4. 2) 4H2O for four O. 3) That gives 8 H, so 4H2. 4) Recheck.
coach.checkApproach: If you have 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2 you are balanced.
coach.findMistake: Never change H2O to H4O or similar; that is a different substance. Only coefficients change.

problem.title: Coefficient of oxygen in propane combustion
problem.statement: Balance C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O and give the coefficient of O2.
hints: Balance C first, then H, then O last.

steps.label: Concept
steps.content: Conservation of mass; O balanced last

commonMistakes.description: Counted O as 7 and wrote 3.5 or 7.
Balanced O before H and got 4.

coach.hint: Carbon and hydrogen come from one molecule each, so fix them first.
coach.concept: Combustion: hydrocarbon plus oxygen gives CO2 and water. Oxygen appears in three places, so balance it last.
coach.guide: 1) 3CO2. 2) 4H2O. 3) Count O on the right: 6 + 4 = 10. 4) 5O2.
coach.checkApproach: If you have 3CO2 and 4H2O, count the oxygen atoms on the right.
coach.findMistake: If you reached 3.5 you counted oxygen atoms as 7; it is 6 from CO2 plus 4 from H2O = 10.

problem.title: Mass conserved in a reaction
problem.statement: When 24 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen it forms 40 g of magnesium oxide. What mass of oxygen reacted?
hints: Mass of reactants equals mass of products.

steps.label: Formula
steps.content: Mass of reactants = mass of products

steps.label: Verify
steps.content: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO: 48 g Mg with 32 g O2 gives 80 g MgO, scaled by half matches

coach.hint: Total mass before equals total mass after. What is missing on the reactant side?
coach.concept: Conservation of mass: atoms rearrange but the total mass stays the same.
coach.guide: 1) Reactants: Mg + O2. 2) Product: MgO. 3) 24 + m = 40. 4) Solve.
coach.checkApproach: If you set 24 + m = 40 you are right.
coach.findMistake: Adding 24 and 40 confuses reactants with products. Oxygen is a reactant, so subtract.
